ὁρᾷν, ἀλλὰ καὶ τὰ ἄλ λως ἔχοντα, ἢ ὡς τὸ ἐν τούτοις τεχνικὸν βούλεται· οὕτω νοῦ
ἔργον ἐστὶ τά τε ἐπιτυγχανόμενα ἐννοήματα θεωρεῖν, καὶ τὰ μὴ, εἴπως αὐτός τε ὑπὸ
τῆς ἐν τοῖς ψεύδεσι πιθανότητος οὐχ ἁλώσεται, καὶ τοὺς ἁλόντας ῥύσεται, ἐὰν νοήσῃ
καὶ τῶν ἄλλων σοφῶν τὰς ῥήσεις, εἴπου σοφίζονται, καὶ τίνα τρόπον

pass_a_gloss: …his truth — or not of these only, but also of those whose craftiness God will seize? For the word has also named these wise. For why will the one spoken of understand the sayings of the blessed wise, yet not be equal to understanding also the words of the remaining wise, but will have a mind lesser than the mind of the wise of this world, and unable to follow the things said by those? And is it not perhaps just as it is a work of an eye not only to see the things set in order, but also the things otherwise disposed, or as the craft in these wishes; so it is a work of mind to contemplate both the thoughts that hit the mark and those that do not, if somehow he himself will not be caught by the persuasiveness in falsehoods, and will rescue those caught, if he understands also the sayings of the other wise, wherever they play the wise, and in what manner they reason falsely; and how the sophism is loosed, and the false reasoning is exposed. For thus also through his own wise God threatens that he will set aside the wisdom of the wise that deserves to perish through falsehood, and the deceptive understanding of those not intelligent according to him, and thus through his own he will seize the craftiness of the wise of this age. At once the disciples of the Lord, if they did not understand the sayings of the worldly wise, how did they campaign toward casting down strongholds, casting down reasonings and every height lifting itself against the knowledge of God? And how would someone also keep perfectly what is said by Peter, Be ready always toward a defense to everyone asking you a word about the hope in you, if he does not have perfectly the preparation in word, so as to be ready toward a defense about the hope in him to every Greek and every barbarian, and every wise and every senseless one, by understanding the sayings of the wise, accusing some, overturning others, and establishing and proving these? And do not wonder if now the one truly wise according to God is not found; for most of the exceptional gifts have failed, so as to be found either not at all or rarely. It remains also to give what the riddles are. And I think a riddle to be a certain extended account about things as having come to be that have not come to be, nor are able to come to be, yet signifying in hiddenness something unspeakable; for example as from a sample that in Judges: Going, the woods went to anoint a king over themselves. For which three fruit-bearing trees — the fig, the vine, the olive — not wishing to reign over the trees not worthy of their kingship; and what the thorny bramble is that sends fire from itself to eat the cedars of Lebanon — it belongs to the wise to see, referring these to the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit, and the bramble to the opposing one. And there is also in Kingdoms such a riddle: The thorn in Lebanon sent toward the Cedar in Lebanon saying: Give your daughter to my son as wife, and the things following. And you would also find in the prophets riddles, as in Ezekiel: The great eagle, the long-winged, the long in stretch, full of feathers, and the things following. So much we have been able to hold for the present toward what lies before us; and these were parable and dark saying, sayings of wise men and riddles. A parable is a speech as concerning something that came to be that did not come to be according to the letter, yet is able to come to be, figuratively indicative of riddles, as The sower went out to sow; for it did not come to be according to the wording, even if it is led up into other things. And how does Open my mouth in parables fit this? For what he brought on has come to be: Before their fathers he did wonders. And according to the letter he split a sea and led them through; for all things have come to be, even if they are symbols of the modes of gospel parables toward which they were led up. But someone else will say that Open my mouth in parables is not referred upon the things from Exodus, but upon the parables in the Gospel of Christ speaking in the prophet: Attend, my people, to my law, and the things upon it. A crown of graces. The circuit of the virtues, because they have been bound to one another. A golden collar about your neck. He calls a golden collar the surrounding radiance and the circular gleam of the divine oracles. And he calls neck the mind. Let us lift his memory from earth. And those who said This is the heir; come, let us kill him, so that the inheritance may become ours, would also say these things. And cast your lot among us. Having stood away from that citizenship, become with us, sabbath with us, do the unleavened things with us, and the other observances of the law. For they themselves are the ones sharing in murder.
pass_b_english: …his truth — or not of these alone, but also of those whose craftiness God will seize? For the word has named those people wise too. Why should the hearer understand the sayings of the blessed wise, yet not stretch to the words of the other wise, and have a mind smaller than the mind of this world wise, unable to follow what they say?

Is it not as with the eye, whose work is not only to see what is in order but also what is otherwise — or as craft wishes in such cases — so also with the mind: its work is to contemplate both thoughts that hit and thoughts that miss, so that it is not caught by the persuasiveness in falsehoods, and so that it can rescue those who are caught, if it also understands the sayings of the other wise wherever they play at wisdom, how they reason falsely, how the sophism is loosed, and how the false reasoning is exposed. That is how, through his own wise, God threatens to set aside wisdom that deserves to perish because of falsehood, and the deceptive understanding of those not intelligent according to him, and so through his own he will seize the craftiness of this age wise.

At once: if the Lord disciples did not understand the sayings of worldly wise people, how did they campaign to cast down strongholds, casting down reasonings and every height that lifts itself against the knowledge of God? And how could anyone keep Peter word perfectly — Always be ready to give a defense to everyone who asks you a word about the hope in you — without full preparation in speech, so as to be ready to defend that hope before every Greek and barbarian, every wise and senseless person, by understanding wise sayings, accusing some, overturning others, and establishing and proving these? Do not wonder if the one truly wise according to God is hard to find now; most of the exceptional gifts have failed, so they appear either not at all or rarely.

It remains to say what riddles are. I take a riddle to be an extended account about things as if they happened that did not happen and cannot happen, yet that signify something unspeakable in hiddenness. Sample from Judges: The trees went to anoint a king over themselves. Which three fruit trees — fig, vine, olive — refused to reign over trees unworthy of their kingship, and what is the thorny bramble that sends fire from itself to eat Lebanon cedars — the wise person sees, referring these to Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, and the bramble to the opposing one. In Kingdoms there is such a riddle too: The thorn in Lebanon sent to the Cedar in Lebanon, saying, Give your daughter to my son as wife, and what follows. In the prophets you also find riddles, as in Ezekiel: The great eagle, long-winged, long in stretch, full of feathers, and what follows.

So much we could hold for now toward what is before us: parable and dark saying, sayings of the wise and riddles. A parable is speech as about something that happened which did not happen according to the letter yet could happen, pointing figuratively to riddles — as The sower went out to sow, which did not happen by the wording even if it is led up into other things. And how does Open my mouth in parables fit? What he added did happen: Before their fathers he did wonders. According to the letter he split a sea and led them through; all of it happened, even if those events are symbols of the modes of gospel parables. Someone else will say Open my mouth in parables is not aimed at Exodus but at Christ parables in the Gospel, as he speaks in the prophet: Attend, my people, to my law, and what follows.

A crown of graces: the circuit of the virtues, because they are bound to one another. A golden collar about your neck: he calls the golden collar the surrounding radiance and circular gleam of the divine oracles, and he calls the neck the mind. Let us lift his memory from earth. Those who said This is the heir; come, let us kill him so the inheritance may be ours would also say this. Cast your lot among us: leave that way of life, be with us, keep sabbath with us, keep the unleavened rites with us, and the other law observances. For they themselves share in the murder.
